prime.problem: Long context hurts three ways at once: the KV cache grows linearly (3 sequences of 128k fit on an H100, none of 1M), every decode step reads all of it, and prefill attention grows with T² (97% of the FLOPs at 1M tokens, ~600 s on one GPU).
prime.fits: Last card. Earlier cards shrank bytes per token or shared them; this one attacks the length itself. It reuses online softmax (ring attention's merge), GQA's KV accounting and KV quantization's capacity arithmetic.
expect: sliding window W and the rolling buffer (slot = i mod W)
ring attention: rotate KV blocks, merge with online softmax
NSA: compressed, selected and window branches
prime.goal: Say which of the three long-context costs each method cuts, compute a window's cache, ring's minimum block size and NSA's tokens read, and choose among them.

attend: Which of the three costs (KV stored, KV read per step, prefill FLOPs) does each of window, ring and NSA actually reduce?
How can information travel further than W tokens in a sliding-window model, and why is that reach only an upper bound?
Why does ring attention stay exact even though each host sees the KV blocks in a different order?
Why does the overlap condition c ≥ F/B not depend on the hidden size d?
Why does NSA still store the whole cache even though it reads only a few thousand tokens per step?

must: Each layer attends only to the last W tokens → the cache is a W-slot rolling buffer → storage and reads stop growing with context (0.54 GB per sequence at any length for a 4,096 window) → far tokens are reachable only indirectly, through stacked layers (≤ W × layers)

Split the sequence over N hosts → each keeps its query block and passes KV blocks around a ring → partial results merge with online softmax's (m, ℓ) in any order → exact attention with 1/N of the KV and compute per host → only if compute per step hides the transfer: block c ≥ F/B tokens

Train sparsity in: a compressed branch, top-n selected 64-token blocks and a recent window, mixed by gates → each step reads s/16 + 1,536 tokens → decode reads 11.6× fewer at 64k (memory-bound, so ≈ that speedup) → but any old block may be selected, so the full cache stays stored
elevated: NSA's selection is block-wise and shared by all query heads in a GQA group → contiguous 64-token loads, one KV fetch per group → sparsity that GPUs can actually exploit (random token gathers would not be)
reference: Mistral's W = 3 vs W = 4 figure mismatch
ring attention's max-context table per device count
NSA's l, d, l′, n, w constants (32, 16, 64, 16, 512)
the H100 NVLink one-way bandwidth reading (450 GB/s)

compress.prompt: Draw a 3 × 3 grid from memory: rows window, ring, NSA; columns KV stored, KV read per decode step, prefill attention FLOPs. Mark each cell cut, split or unchanged, with one number where you remember one.
checklist: window: stored cut, read cut, prefill attention cut (W per token), at a reach cost
ring: stored and FLOPs split across devices, total unchanged; exact
NSA: stored unchanged, read cut (s/16 + 1,536), must be trained in
the overlap condition c ≥ F/B for ring
none of them makes one H100 hold a 1M-token full-attention cache

retrieve.q: Explain why ring attention is not a way to shrink the KV cache.
answer: the total KV is the same as full attention (137.4 GB at 1M tokens for Llama-3.1-8B)
it distributes it: each of N hosts holds 1/N
it removes the single-device limit, not the bytes

retrieve.q: Walk through one ring step on host i: what it computes, what it sends, what it receives, and how the result stays exact.
answer: compute blockwise attention of its query block against the KV block it holds
send that KV block to host i+1 while receiving one from host i−1
update its running (m, ℓ, O) with online softmax
after N steps every query block has met every KV block; order doesn't matter

retrieve.q: A product needs 128k-token contexts for Llama-3.1-8B-sized models on H100s. Compare adding a sliding window, adopting an NSA-trained model and using ring attention, by what each costs you.
answer: window: 119 sequences instead of 3, but far tokens only reachable indirectly, and adding it post hoc isn't what Mistral tested
NSA: 13.5× fewer bytes read per step, but still 3 sequences stored and it must be pretrained in
ring: exact and splits prefill across devices, but needs N GPUs with fast links and doesn't shrink decode reads

retrieve.q: Where does ring attention stop hiding its communication, and what does the paper's A100 InfiniBand row say about slow links?
answer: each host's block must be at least F/B tokens, and it holds 6 blocks, so s ≥ 6c per host
A100 InfiniBand (12.5 GB/s): c ≈ 25K, s ≈ 150K tokens per host before communication hides

compare.q: Ring attention merges partial attention results from different hosts; online softmax merged partial sums from different threads. What is the same, and what does ring attention have to overlap that online softmax didn't?
answer: same: each partial carries (m, ℓ) (plus O), and ⊕ merges them exactly in any order
ring must also overlap moving KV blocks between hosts with compute
hence the c ≥ F/B condition; within one GPU the data is already there

compare.q: Course 7 calls ring attention context parallelism (CP), one of four training dimensions. Why is it a training and prefill tool more than a decode tool?
answer: it splits attention FLOPs and activations for long sequences, which dominate training and prefill
decode is bound by bytes read per step, which ring doesn't reduce
for decode, engines shard the KV (perf-2) or shrink it

predict.q: Take NSA's budget to 256k tokens. How many tokens does one decode step read, and what is the expected decode speedup? Then: for ring attention over a 400 Gbps (50 GB/s) link between H100s, what is the minimum block size and tokens per host? Commit first.
predict.answer: NSA: 262,144 / 16 + 1,536 = 17,920 tokens, so about 14.6× fewer bytes read than full attention. Only the compressed branch grows with length. Ring: c ≥ 989e12 / 50e9 ≈ 19.8K tokens per block, and 6c ≈ 119K tokens per host before communication hides behind compute (our arithmetic).
